note: AutoTone clips 1% at each end of the luma histogram instead of 0.1%, so a clean ramp gets a black point above 0, caught by AutoToneTests.rampIsIdentity
AutoTone averages an empty bright set, so an all-black buffer's white balance is NaN, caught by AutoToneTests.blackSuggestsIdentity
AutoTone inverts the levels gamma ratio, so a median at a quarter of the span gets gamma 0.5 instead of 2, caught by AutoToneTests.levelsStretchAndCentreMedian
AutoTone white balance keeps pixels with a channel at 0 or 1, so clamped bright highlights skew the balance, caught by AutoToneTests.clippedHighlightsIgnored
AutoTone white balance averages every pixel instead of the brightest 5%, so a warm highlight over a cool picture is not neutralised, caught by AutoToneTests.balanceReadsBrightestFivePercent
AutoTone white balance drops the slider clamp, so an extreme cast suggests a temperature past -100 that whiteBalance refuses, caught by AutoToneTests.extremeCastClampsToSliderRange
